title: runtime probe matrix: unified prefill/decode scheduling telemetry
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: produce a low-overhead, correlated telemetry surface (the 'probe matrix') that lets us attribute end-to-end latency and cost between prefill scheduler decisions, decode-time kernel selection, and attention routing. This ticket designs and implements an initial shipping MVP: (1) lightweight NVTX envelopes from GPU kernels with a compact tag payload, (2) matching CPU-side OpenTelemetry spans emitted by the request scheduler and kernel dispatcher, and (3) a set of per-kernel metrics and derived request-level aggregates exposed to Grafana/Prometheus for debugging and regressions. Motivation: recent customer incidents show intermittent tail latency spikes that are not explainable from request QPS alone — we need per-request visibility into scheduling delays, selection mismatches, and attention-path costs. The probe matrix will help us: - correlate kernel choice vs. observed exec_time and queue_wait - quantify prefill vs decode scheduling latencies per request - detect suboptimal attention heuristics (e.g., when attention-path falls back to generic kernel) - compute request-level GPU token-cost estimates for billing/debugging
acceptance_criteria: 1) Runtime emits NVTX ranges with compact tags (request_id, stage, kernel_hint) for prefill & decode kernels; 2) Scheduler emits OpenTelemetry spans that include the same request_id and stage tags; 3) New prometheus metrics are registered: runtime_kernel_exec_ms_bucket, runtime_kernel_queue_ms_sum, runtime_prefill_schedule_delay_ms_sum; 4) Grafana dashboard shows a trace-linked panel demonstrating correlation across CPU span -> NVTX range -> per-kernel metric for at least three representative workloads (short-chat, long-chat, batched-embeddings); 5) End-to-end telemetry overhead <= 2% p50 latency increase at scale (validated on canary).
tasks: Design tag schema for NVTX envelopes (max 64 bytes): request_id (16b truncated UUID), stage={prefill,decode}, kernel_hint, token_range
Add lightweight span context propagation to scheduler + dispatcher (avoid heap allocs on hot path)
Implement per-kernel counters (exec_ms/histogram + queue_ms/histogram) with per-request labels where feasible (sampling)
Create Grafana dashboard prototype and Prometheus alert for sudden rise in kernel_queue_ms p95
Run canary load tests to measure overhead and false positives from sampling
Document instrumentation contract for future kernel authors
design_notes: We intentionally avoid heavy tracing on every token boundary. Instead we use: - deterministic, compact NVTX envelope written at kernel launch and kernel completion; - sampled per-request OpenTelemetry spans at 5% by default, configurable per-customer; - aggregate counters for continuous monitoring and histograms for distribution. Trade-offs: higher sampling improves attribution but increases overhead and cardinality. To limit cardinality we keep request_id truncated in metrics and use labels only for sampled traces. For full attribution during an incident, we'll use distributed tracing (sampled) and correlate with full request logs via request_id.
implementation_decisions: 1) NVTX payload format: <trunc_uuid:16>|<stage:1>|<kernel_hint:8>|<tok_start:2>|<tok_end:2> (packed bytes base64) — compact, fixed width. 2) Emit NVTX ranges only on kernel entry/exit (no token-level NVTX in hot path). 3) Scheduler will call a lock-free writer to append a small 'probe record' to an in-process ring buffer that the telemetry flusher reads asynchronously. 4) Prometheus metrics use exemplar support (where available) to attach trace_id to histogram samples for easier linking.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: added NVTX calls could change GPU kernel timing if misused. Mitigation: keep NVTX payload writes off the GPU submission hot path using cached buffer writes. Risk: cardinality blowup in Prometheus. Mitigation: sample traces and only attach request_id as exemplar; use derived aggregates for SLOs. Risk: mismatch between CPU span names and NVTX tags causing correlation gaps. Mitigation: enforce a shared tag schema library and unit tests that validate roundtrip correlation.
testing_plan: Unit tests for tag packing/unpacking; integration test that runs three workloads locally and validates that a single request generates: CPU span -> NVTX entry -> NVTX exit -> per-kernel metric emission. Load test on staging with 10k RPS equivalent to detect overhead; compare p50/p95 with and without instrumentation. Blackbox test: run a synthetic scenario that intentionally forces attention fallback and assert dashboard shows increased kernel_exec_ms for fallback kernel.
